newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House interior bill keeps SPR sale.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House interior bill keeps SPR sale.

text.p: A measure to sell $209 million of oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve will stay in a House interior spending bill, but lawmakers have agreed to remove the sale later when they mesh the House and Senate bills, a spokeswoman for Rep. Dan Schaefer said Thursday.
"All parties have agreed that this will be knocked out in conference," said the spokeswoman for the Colorado Republican. Schaefer chairs the House Commerce Energy subcommittee.
Schaefer had asked the House Rules Committee to move to strike the SPR sale from a $13 billion interior spending bill, saying his panel had not authorized the sale.
But Democrats, embroiled in a fight with Republicans over another measure in the interior bill, objected to Schaefer's request.
The House was in the process of debating the rule on the interior bill, which says which amendment can be considered and which provisions should be stricken.
